module purpose: neorv32_cpu_pmp stores PMP configuration and address registers through CSR writes, returns those registers on CSR reads, selects the current fetch or load/store access context, checks it against the configured regions and permissions, and outputs a registered fault flag.

use-case flows.value: CSR write decoding and storage of per-region PMP policy bytes (R/W/X, address-matching mode, lock)
CSR write decoding and storage of per-region PMP address registers
Packed PMP policy or address readback on csr_o, selected by CSR address
Per-region lock state that blocks later pmpcfg/pmpaddr writes and removes machine-mode bypass in permission checks
Selection of fetch or load/store access context, region address matching, permission evaluation, and fail-chain computation
Registered PMP fault report on fault_o, suppressed in debug mode
PMP policy, address, derived mask, and fault report forced to zero while rstn_i='0'

conceptual assets.concept: CSR write-target decision for PMP configuration and address registers
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flows first decode CSR address and write intent into one-hot write-enable decisions at lines 113-114 and 157-158, and those decisions gate the actual state updates at lines 127 and 170. Integrity is established because a wrong decision would update the wrong PMP entry or suppress an intended update; availability is also established because the one-hot decision is produced whenever the addressed CSR write condition holds.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-region PMP policy state: execute, read, write, address-matching mode, and lock bits
conceptual assets.reasoning: Per-region policy bytes are written from CSR data into pmpcfg at lines 127-145, with invalid address-matching modes forced off at lines 134-140 and reserved bits cleared at line 143. This stored policy is read back through lines 203, 236, and 190, blocks later configuration/address writes at lines 127 and 170-172, controls mask generation at lines 266-269, selects region-match behavior at lines 303-312, and determines execute/read/write permission at lines 323-339, so integrity of the stored policy is established; availability is established by held state and CSR readback.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-region PMP address and boundary state
conceptual assets.reasoning: Per-region address registers are written from CSR data at lines 170-176 only when the target entry is unlocked and TOR chaining permits the update. The stored address state is returned on csr_o through lines 205-223 and 192, and it is used to build NAPOT masks at line 257 and to compare the checked address against region bounds at lines 285, 295, and 296, so integrity of the stored boundary state is established; availability is established by held state and CSR readback.

conceptual assets.concept: Selected access context under PMP check
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes the current checked context by selecting the address at line 244 (`pc_nxt` for instruction-side checks, else `addr_ls_i`) and the privilege source at line 245 (`cpu_priv` for instruction-side checks, else `lsu_priv`). Later comparisons and permission/fault logic consume this selected context at lines 285, 295, 296, 322, 329, 336, and 351, so integrity of the selected access context is established; availability is combinational under the shown selection conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-region address-match decision for the selected access
conceptual assets.reasoning: For each region, match_gen turns the selected address comparisons and configured mode into a match decision: TOR uses the compare results at lines 303-307, NAPOT uses `cmp_na` at lines 309-310, and other modes force no match at line 312. The fail chain at line 354 depends on this decision, so integrity of the region-match result is established; availability is combinational whenever the compared values and mode are present.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-region access-permission decision for execute, read, or write
conceptual assets.reasoning: perm_gen computes permission from access kind, privilege, lock state, and the R/W/X bits: execute at lines 321-325, read at lines 328-332, and write at lines 335-339, with machine-mode bypass only when the lock bit is clear. The violation chain uses this result at line 354, so integrity of the permission decision is established; availability is combinational under the shown branches.

The module computes the violation/report result with the default non-machine-mode fallback at line 351, the matched-region reduction at line 354, and the registered output `fault_o <= (not ctrl_i.cpu_debug) and fail(0)` at line 363. Integrity is established because the reported fault must follow the computed violation and debug-suppression condition exactly; availability is established when `rstn_i = '1'` and a clock edge occurs.
